story.value: Strontium is named after Strontian, a town in Scotland.
Strontium was first isolated by the English chemist Humphry Davy in 1808.
In 1790, Adair Crawford recognized a new mineral, strontianite, as different from other barium minerals.

uses.value: Strontium is used in making color television picture tubes.
Strontium is combined with iron to make magnets.
Strontium carbonate, a strontium compound, is used to make certain kinds of glass.
Strontium has found use in refining zinc.
